title: Twisted yarn over
subtitle: A yarn over worked through the back loop to close the eyelet and add a firm increase.
excerpt: The twisted yarn over is a yarn over that is knitted through the back loop on the following row, closing the eyelet that a standard yarn over would leave. It adds one stitch invisibly in situations where a yarn over increase is wanted without the decorative hole.
sourceNotes: The twisted yarn over is documented in Mary Thomas's Knitting Book (1938) as a method for adding stitches without creating a deliberate eyelet. Used in traditional European and Scandinavian knitting techniques where a closed increase is needed.
heroPrompt: Close-up of a knitted swatch showing a column of twisted yarn overs worked into a stocking stitch fabric, the increases nearly invisible compared to an adjacent column of standard yarn overs.

glossaryTerms.definition: A yarn over that is worked through the back loop on the return row, twisting the new stitch closed and preventing the decorative eyelet that a standard yarn over creates.

An increase worked by wrapping the yarn around the right needle. On the following row the new loop is worked as a stitch. When worked through the front loop it leaves a small decorative hole; worked through the back loop it closes the hole.

content.text: (yo) wraps the yarn around the right needle and creates a new stitch with a small eyelet below it, which is the basis of lace knitting. The

uses the same wrap but closes the resulting loop by working it through the back loop on the following row, eliminating the eyelet. The result is a single added stitch that blends nearly invisibly into the fabric. It appears in patterns that require increases on right-side rows without decorative holes, and in some continental and traditional European knitting traditions as a standard increase method. Difficulty: intermediate.
DK or any smooth yarn (the twist is easier to see on a plain, smooth fibre)
Needles in the appropriate size for the yarn
Work to the point where the increase is needed.
Bring the yarn over the top of the right needle from front to back (the standard yarn over motion). Continue working the row.
On the return (wrong-side) row, work across in pattern until you reach the yarn over from the previous row.
Insert the needle into the back leg of the yarn over loop (through the back loop) and purl it. This twists the stitch closed, eliminating the eyelet.
On the following row, knit the newly formed stitch normally. It should sit neatly in the fabric without a hole below it.

attrs.title: In-the-round variation
attrs.body: When working in the round, the yarn over sits on the needle for one round before being worked. On the next round, knit the yarn over through the back loop (k1tbl) to close the hole. The principle is the same; the direction of the twist adjusts for the absence of a wrong-side row.

content.text: The twisted yarn over appears in patterns that increase on right-side rows without a decorative eyelet: the gusset increases of some traditional sock patterns, the side increases of seamless top-down raglan yokes, and any textured panel where an increase is required but a lace hole would be out of place. Some European-tradition patterns write 'yo, k1tbl' or 'yo tbl' as a standard increase abbreviation.

items.symptom: A hole remains after working through the back loop
items.cause: The stitch was worked through the front loop rather than the back
items.fix: Re-check which loop is the back leg. On a standard yarn over that has not been twisted, the right leg of the loop faces toward you (front); the left leg faces away (back). Insert the needle into the back leg.

items.symptom: The twisted stitch is very tight and difficult to work on the following row
items.cause: The yarn over was too snug
items.fix: Allow slightly more yarn when making the yarn over. The twist adds tension; the loop needs a little extra give to work comfortably.

items.symptom: The increase is visible as a small bump rather than blending into the fabric
items.cause: The stitch mounted correctly but the yarn over was in a different direction from the surrounding stitches
items.fix: Check that the yarn over was wrapped in the standard direction. A backward yarn over mounts with reversed legs, which can look different even when worked through the back loop.
